public_evidence.title: Movement at the relay
public_evidence.text: Shelter B reports unusual movement outside its perimeter. The report does not establish where it began.

public_evidence.title: A one-way sighting
public_evidence.text: A road camera confirms a zombie group moving B → D. It cannot identify the group's earlier route.

public_evidence.title: Emergency at the infirmary
public_evidence.text: D sends its first emergency transmission. D is now visibly Overrun; no other shelter is visibly Overrun.

public_evidence.title: Timestamps are incomplete
public_evidence.text: Emergency transmissions may arrive up to four minutes late. Quiet shelters may already be Exposed. Only Overrun status is public.

diagnostic_evidence.title: The camera clock was wrong
diagnostic_evidence.text: Recovered camera metadata places unusual activity inside D at 10:02, before the first confirmed B → D movement at 10:05. The recording is incomplete: it does not identify the first infected person or rule out an earlier arrival from elsewhere. Reconsider whether B's sighting proves B was the source.

ground_truth_timeline.text: The original outbreak begins inside D, the old infirmary.
Pre-mission contacts leave B, C, E and G Exposed. D becomes Overrun. These historical contacts are not extra gameplay edges.
Unusual activity inside D is recorded on a camera with a miscalibrated clock.
B reports movement. A report's location is not proof of origin.
Zombies travel B → D. This is a real sighting, but not the initiating infection of D.
D's delayed emergency reaches the team. The three-round containment mission begins.
